gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ALLPOWERS has sold two S2000 Pro generations with different solar inputs: the older manual gives 650 W at 18–70 V and 18 A max and includes an XT60-to-MC4 cable, while the AP-SS-009-PRO manual gives 1,000 W at 12–150 V and lists no solar cable in the box. ALLPOWERS's own S2000 Pro + SF200 kit listing still describes the 650 W unit, while its S2000 Pro + 100 W kit listing says 1,000 W.
standout_why: I compared powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited, 28 kits with a station solar-spec table) and stormwatts.com same-panel-watts (cited, 24 kits with wiring rules). Both give BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and AC180 input limits and SP200L Voc, and StormWatts covers two panels in series vs parallel on the Elite 200 V2. Neither covers any ALLPOWERS kit or the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini, and neither mentions station generations or firmware. bluettipower.com/pages/solar-generator (cited) returned HTTP 429, so I could not compare it.
decides: It affects the second pick, not the first. Under $700 at link price, the largest-battery kit that ships now is the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SE100 ($673.74 link, $748.60 store, 1,451 Wh). The page should give that kit's solar limit as the 1,000 W / 12–150 V figure from its own listing, and say that the S2000 Pro + SF200 kit ($612.90 link, pre-order to Nov 19) is listed with the older 650 W, 18–70 V description. The shopper should check the model number on the box (AP-SS-009-PRO for the newer unit) before adding panels. The S2000 Pro + 100 W listing gives 43.2 V × 33.6 Ah, which suggests Li-ion rather than LiFePO4; this is my reading, not a stated chemistry, and it matters because ChatGPT told shoppers to prioritise LiFePO4. That supports the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini + 200 W kit ($616.55 link, 1,004.8 Wh) as the ships-now pick for a LiFePO4 buyer. Expansion limit on that kit: BLUETTI's page says 'up to 350W solar', so the kit's one 200 W panel leaves 150 W of headroom, and a second 200 W panel (400 W) would go past the cap. EcoFlow's own DELTA 3 Classic solar-generator kits are all over $700 at EcoFlow US today, so ChatGPT's $659 top pick is not EcoFlow's own store listing.
